tasks.title: LLM client with cache and cost log
tasks.desc: OpenAI-SDK client for https://api.meta.ai/v1 with per-job model routing, response cache keyed by hash(model + prompt), and a cost log with a hard $12/day cap. Done: test proves a repeated prompt hits cache with zero HTTP calls and the cap blocks over-budget calls. Touches: lab2rob/llm/client.py, cache.py, cost_log.py, lab2rob/tests/test_llm.py.

notes.text:
The LLM foundation is implemented and tested: all later stages call the Meta API through this client, never directly.

- New: lab2rob/llm/client.py (job-to-model routing per section 5, cache-first, caps enforced before sending), cache.py (response cache keyed by hash of model + prompt + params, atomic writes), cost_log.py (JSONL ledger of tokens + dollars, hard $12/day cap, $15 hard_case sub-budget). The openai package is imported lazily, so tests and cached paths never need it.
- Tests: lab2rob/tests/test_llm.py, 7 passed in ~5s, fully offline (fake transport). They prove a repeated prompt costs zero extra calls, the cache key covers model and params, the daily cap refuses over-budget calls before sending, routing matches the section-5 table, and the ledger survives reopening.
- Design note: call cost is known only after sending, so the daily cap can overshoot by at most one call; spend that happened is always logged (force-recorded).

Needs you in a normal terminal (my sandbox user cannot write to your conda env): `conda activate lab2rob`, then `pip install openai`, and set MODEL_API_KEY. Until then live calls raise a clear error telling you exactly that; FD-02's done-checks (cache + cap tests) all pass without them.

To check: `conda activate lab2rob && python -m pytest lab2rob/tests/ -q` from the repo root. This unblocks IG-04 once approved.

tasks.desc: Predicate library (in_slot, capped, volume, concentration, no_spill, ...) plus the synonym lexicon with ontology ids (Eppendorf to tube_1_5ml, spin to centrifuge, ...). notes.text:
Predicates, lexicon, and the status taxonomy are done; the registry now knows what exists, what expands, and what is merely named.

- Predicates (lab2rob/registry/predicates.py): in_slot, capped, lid_open, volume, concentration, no_spill over a documented plain-dict state protocol. Total functions: missing keys fail with an explanation, never raise. Tests: 7 pass/fail/robustness tests on fake states.
- Lexicon (lab2rob/registry/lexicon.yaml + index loader): 60 entries mapping protocol words to canonical skills/objects (eppendorf, spin, pcr, 96-well plate...), case-insensitive, duplicate synonyms rejected loudly. ontology_id field present but null everywhere: IDs need OBI/ChEBI/UO lookups with network access, and I would not guess them.
- Status taxonomy: every skill/asset carries implemented | macro | declared. skills.yaml stays generated (overlays macros.yaml + declared.yaml merged by an extended generator scanning all four biolab API files); assets.yaml is hand-maintained. Counts: 20 implemented skills, 3 macros (transfer, mix_by_pipetting, serial_dilution — validated to bottom out in aspirate/dispense), 32 declared skills, 16 implemented assets (pipette, plates, reservoirs, dishes added), 15 declared objects. resolve_skill/resolve_asset give the grounder its mapping: declared -> out_of_scope/not_implemented, unknown -> unknown_skill/unknown_asset. A note on IG-03 points the grounder at it (no grounder exists yet to update directly).
- Two corrections worth knowing: (1) FD-04 had missed the Protein/Culture/Drug Api classes — the generator now scans protein.py, culture.py and drug.py too, which is also what makes transfer-family macros honest. (2) change_tip is declared, not a macro: the simulated pipette has no tip state, so no honest expansion exists. Say the word if you want motion-pantomime expansions instead — I recommend against.
- Tests: 34 passed total (13 new/updated registry + predicate tests), plus --check green.

To check: `python lab2rob/registry/gen_skills.py --check` and `python -m pytest lab2rob/tests/ -q`. Unblocks IG-03, SC-01, SC-02 once approved.

The lab2rob CLI works end to end: compile grounds a protocol (optional auto-accept of grounded steps), certify builds and certifies a decided session, eval runs a sandboxed agent from a JSON spec on a certified run (scripted/policy/zero-shot, twin labels, instruction override), and report writes funnel.json, audit.json, metrics.json and report.md under runs/<report_id>/report/. The audit follows SciHorizon buckets (first pass, auto-recovered, human-fixed, plus rejected/still-open) with the rules documented in the markdown. Verified: 231 pytest green (6 new CLI/report tests incl. a live sim chain and golden audit fixtures), registry check green. notes.text:
The ingest-to-ground pilot runs end to end on 3 real BioProt protocols: 13 steps in, every one grounded, out-of-scope with a reason, or ambiguous — zero LLM calls needed.

- Ingest: lab2rob/ingest/bioprot.py loads lab2rob/ingest/sources/tier1_protocols.json (moved there from lab2rob/) into RawProtocol objects (verbatim raw text, source URL, license, human hints attached but never parsed) plus Task skeletons; BioProt-repo-by-id is an explicit NotImplementedError stub for later.
- Rules (lab2rob/ground/rules.py): strips None/Namount/reagents noise, keeps NOTES as comments, joins continuations; pint quantities (µL/M/mg/mL/%, ~ flags, case-normalized units); reagent heads; earliest lexicon verb (multi-word aware); verdict priority ambiguity/pH patterns -> verb mapping -> 1 mL pipette-capacity / 36 mL vessel checks -> grounded, else needs_llm. 4 verb synonyms added to the lexicon (dissolve, weigh, add, make up).
- LLM fallback (lab2rob/ground/llm_ground.py): schema-validated JSON, one retry, then ambiguous; proven offline with a fake transport.
- Report (python -m lab2rob.ground.report): 1779 CTAB mix: 1 grounded (transfer 75 uL) + 3 out-of-scope (mix/dilute declared, 12.5 mL exceeds pipette with no pour primitive); 1780 sodium acetate: 3 out-of-scope (incl. pH titration unmodeled) + 1 ambiguous (aliquot size); 1778 SDS buffer: 3 out-of-scope + 2 ambiguous (prepare-stock without amounts); storage/thermal description flags on 1779/1778.
- vs the human hints: two principled divergences. Action status is checked before vessel size, so make-up-to-50/500 mL steps report not_implemented (dilute is declared) rather than missing_asset; and 12.5 mL transfer reports missing_skill (no pour primitive beyond 1 mL pipetting) rather than missing_asset. A test proves stripping the hints never changes grounding.
- Tests: 54 passed (20 new). Bugs caught by the suite: a missing paren, µL codepoint lookup, unit case (mL vs ml), Grounding field name in a message.

To check: `python -m pytest lab2rob/tests/ -q` and `python -m lab2rob.ground.report`. Needs pint in the env (already installed). This validates the IG-02/IG-03 approach on real data; scaling to 30 protocols + WLP scoring stays in those tasks.

tasks.title: Fix empty LLM replies starving grounding
tasks.desc: Full-LLM translation and single-step fallback fail with not-JSON char 0 because the model spends about 1022 of the 1024 max_tokens budget reasoning and returns empty text; the empty replies are then cached and replayed forever. Fix: explicit per-call token budgets (single step 2048, full translation scaled by step count), never cache or serve empty-text responses, and report token counts on failure. Done: regression tests green and full-LLM translation returns verdicts in the browser. Touches lab2rob/llm/, lab2rob/ground/, tests.

notes.text: Plan: explicit max_tokens on grounding calls (single step 2048, full 2048 + 128/step capped at 8192); cache treats empty-text responses as misses and never stores them; failure details carry completion/reasoning token counts. Regression tests in test_llm.py + test_ground_llm.py.

Full-LLM translation should work now: grounding calls get explicit token budgets (single step 2048, full translation 2048 plus 128 per step up to 8192) so the model has room to reason and answer, and empty replies are never cached or served, which also heals the poisoned cache entries automatically. Failure details now carry completion and reasoning token counts. Verified: 147 pytest green (4 new regression tests). Please check: re-run full-LLM translation on the same protocol in the browser and confirm verdicts come back; the first retry re-sends a few cents of calls the old cache had poisoned. tasks.title: Build declared labware from open asset sources
tasks.desc:
Turns the most-requested declared assets in registry/assets.yaml into buildable ones, so steps that now fail as missing_asset (19 in the 42-protocol sweep) or not_implemented can compile. Done: at least the 96-well plate, 1.5 mL tube, 15/50 mL tubes and a tip rack are status: implemented, built by the scene code, with license and source recorded per asset.

Where the assets come from (researched 2026-10-30):
- Opentrons labware definitions (Apache-2.0, 164 JSON files): exact dimensions for 96/384-well plates, tip racks, Falcon/Eppendorf tube racks. Build them from primitives like scene.py already does. Default for labware.
- AutoBio (MuJoCo MJCF): centrifuges (Tiangen mini, Eppendorf 5430/5910 Ri), vortexer, thermal cycler, thermal mixer, pipette + tip, tip box, 96-well PCR plate, 1.5/15/50 mL tubes, 100 mm dish. No license file (authors' license issue open since Aug 2026).
- ChemLab-Assets (MBZUAI, URDF/USD): CC BY-NC 4.0, flag non-commercial if used.

Decided: AutoBio meshes are allowed for the hackathon demo. Each AutoBio asset is recorded with license "UNLICENSED (AutoBio, demo only)" and excluded from released datasets (export manifest filters it) until the authors publish a license.

notes.text: Decision recorded (human, 2026-10-30): AutoBio meshes allowed for the hackathon demo; kept out of released datasets until licensed.
